description: Cold grey plates with a warm red seam shut inside them. It gives nothing until you cut, and then it takes its share back.
lore: Most soulstones are warm all the way through. This one is warm along a line. The plates are properly cold, colder than the grass it came out of, and the heat is down in the black seams between them, so the way to be sure of one is to close your fist and wait for a single warm line to come up against the palm. Buyers turn them to the light first, hunting the gap where the red shows through. The people who crack for a living gave that habit up years ago. A stone shut tight and a stone with the red on show are the same stone.

It will not be cut. Every tool anyone has taken to one parts it along a seam instead of through it, so it goes into work exactly as it came out of the grass: wired in behind a guard, sunk into a pommel, seated under the lip of a bracer with the plates untouched. Smiths do not mind that. What they pass on to the buyer is the other rule, which is that the setting has to leave the seams open to the air. Shut one into metal on every side and it lies there like a pebble and does nothing at all.

Carrying it is uneventful. It has no opinion about a long march and none about a wait, and it is the plainest thing in the pack right up until the first cut lands. Then it arrives about half a breath late. Whatever you opened, some part of it comes back the other way and closes what it finds. Everyone who has felt it says the same two things in the same order: that it is a great deal of comfort, and that it is not a kindness. Nothing is being given here. Something is being taken and divided.

The last thing worth knowing only shows up when a good many are laid out side by side. Handle enough of any other kind and small disagreements start turning up between them, a shade off, a hair of weight off, one stretch of country to the next. Not these. The same grey, the same plating, the same red shut away the same way, off an animal that has gone unmentioned long enough that most of what it was has already gone with the telling. Whatever it has lost, and it has lost nearly all of it, the bottom of it has not moved. A description of that animal would be out of date by now. The stone is not.
